messages:
From: Peter Klein <peter.klein@orbitsoft.com>

Cc: contracts@orbitsoft.com, ops@orbitsoft.com
Date: Tue, 14 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrbitSoft redlines — Order Form & SLA

Dylan,

Thanks for the draft. We've gone through the Order Form and attached a PDF with our preferred redlines (see OrbitSoft_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf). A few items we want to highlight up front so Legal & Engineering can triage: 

- Uptime target: asking for 99.95% monthly (down from your 99.9% draft).
- Service credits: 10% monthly credit for < 99.95% and scaling to 25% for < 99.5%.
- Response times: P1 15 minutes SLA response (we understand this is aggressive); P2 2 hours.
- Maintenance: no maintenance windows between 08:00–18:00 in their primary region without 72h notice and compensating credits.

We're flexible to discuss exceptions (e.g., for planned major upgrades) but wanted to get these on the table. Please confirm who on your side will drive the redline discussion and if you can provide a quantifiable measurement definition for uptime (monitoring sources, metrics).

Thanks,
Peter
Peter Klein
Head of Infrastructure
OrbitSoft

Peter — thanks for the note and the annotated PDF. Looping in Laura (Legal) and Marcus (SRE/Products) so we can respond concretely. High level reactions: 

- Uptime: 99.95% is a heavier commitment than our standard tiering. We can propose a targeted 99.93% for the first 12 months with a roadmap to 99.95% tied to capacity reservations / dedicated pools. Will Marcus weigh in on feasibility?
- Service credits: can do a capped credit schedule, but our standard cap is 50% annual — we should avoid uncapped exposure.
- P1/P2 response: P1 acknowledgement within 30 minutes, full response plan within 2 hours is what we typically give. 15-minute ack may be hard for our default hosted tier but could be offered with Dedicated.
- Maintenance blackout: we can accept a daytime blackout for customer-facing windows for the primary region with 72h notice, subject to a carve-out for emergency security fixes (with post-facto credits).

Next steps: Laura — can you propose redline language for the Order Form & SLA that captures the above flex (including Dedicated as an option for tighter response/availability)? Marcus — can you produce a short note on measurement sources (edge vs control plane, how we calculate downtime) and what guarantees we can operationally hit in Q3.

I'll sync with Peter after we have proposed language.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Exec, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: OrbitSoft redlines — Order Form & SLA

Dylan / Marcus — drafting suggested redline language below for insertion into the Order Form / Exhibit A (SLA):

1) Uptime measurement: 
   - "Uptime" is calculated as (1 - (TotalMinutesOfDowntime / TotalMinutesInMonth)) * 100, where "Downtime" is determined from Redwood's control-plane telemetry (ingestion & inference endpoints) filtered by OrbitSoft's account ID. Redwood will provide monthly availability reports and allow OrbitSoft read-only access to availability dashboards.

2) SLA tiers & credits: 
   - >= 99.95%: No credit
   - 99.90% — 99.94%: 5% monthly credit
   - 99.00% — 99.89%: 15% monthly credit
   - < 99.00%: 30% monthly credit (capped at one month's fees for the affected product line)
   - Cap: Aggregate annual credits not to exceed 50% of annual subscription fees for the affected product line.

3) Response & remediation windows (definitions): 
   - P1 (Service-down impacting production inference for customer): Acknowledgement within 30 minutes; initial mitigation plan within 2 hours; continuous remediation updates every 2 hours until resolved.
   - P2 (Significant degradation): Acknowledgement within 1 hour; mitigation plan within 6 hours.

4) Maintenance windows & blackout policy: 
   - Planned maintenance: Redwood will provide >=72 hours notice for planned maintenance that may impact availability. Daytime blackout (08:00–18:00 local to OrbitSoft primary region) will be applied for customer-impacting maintenance with the option to schedule outside peak hours.
   - Emergency maintenance: allowed for security-critical fixes; Redwood will notify OrbitSoft as soon as feasible and provide credits per SLA if an emergency maintenance event results in measurable downtime.

5) Exceptions & Dedicated option: 
   - Parties may negotiate a Dedicated Capacity Addendum with stronger guarantees (e.g., 99.97% and 15-minute P1 ack) and different credit caps.

Notes: I framed the credit caps and measurement definition to reduce open financial exposure while providing OrbitSoft clearer remedies. Please confirm if OrbitSoft requires the 15-minute P1 acknowledgement specifically for all environments — if so, we should surface Dedicated as the recommended vehicle.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 15:09:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OrbitSoft redlines — Order Form & SLA

Peter — quick operational note to supplement Laura's draft. Two items to consider for the technical appendix (so measurement is robust and mutually auditable):

- Measurement sources: primary uptime derived from control-plane telemetry + active health checks at the inference endpoint. We'll include a sample query (metric name: redwood.inference.request.success_rate) and the aggregation window used to compute downtime. We'll also provide a weekly raw CSV export for reconciliation on request.

- Maintenance scheduling: to reduce the need for wide blackout windows we can offer a "Regional Maintenance Contract" where OrbitSoft designates a 4-hour weekly maintenance slot (outside core business hours) and gets lower credit exposure and higher availability commitments in exchange. This is an opt-in addendum in the Order Form.

Operational feasibility: With moderate capacity reservations (Committed vCPU/GPU and pre-warming), we can reliably target 99.95% for Q3 for the majority of traffic. 99.97% will require dedicated pools and additional ops headcount on on-call — feasible but more expensive.

If OrbitSoft wants the 15-minute P1 ack across the board, we'd need to route them to a Dedicated support tier with 24x7 primary on-call and an agreed-on runbook (we can attach an SLO operational runbook as an appendix). Happy to hop on a 30-min call with your Ops team to walk the measurement queries and the Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs.

Marcus Lin
Director, SRE & Product Reliability
Redwood Inference
